text_simplified: Children learn important social skills from interacting with their peers, such as sharing, taking turns, and managing emotions. Positive relationships with friends enhance their sense of satisfaction with school and improve academic performance. Children’s ways of interacting with others vary—some are sociable, while others are shy or need time to adjust—and all these differences are natural. A home environment rich in play, activities, and family interactions supports cognitive and linguistic development.

review_defects.why: The Arabic 'الألعاب' means 'toys/games' (concrete objects or structured activities), while the English 'play' refers to the abstract activity of playing. This slightly shifts the meaning from a home rich in toys/games to one rich in play opportunities.
